From Jim Leonard (trixter -at- oldskool.org)

Here you go.  I made these myself, and made sure to flex all of the 
PCX format's CGA attributes.  These all load perfectly under *REAL* 
PC Paintbrush 4.0 in DOS on a CGA card, so if your decoder screws it 
up, it's the fault of your decoder!

They are:

CGA_FSD.PCX    Standard lightcyan-lightmagenta-white palette (intensity 
bit set) with black background.  When most people think of CGA, they're 
thinking of this.

CGA_TST1.PCX    Different palette (intensite bit NOT set) and different 
background color.  If you can read the text inside the box at the bottom, 
your decoder is shite :-)

CGA_RGBI.PCX    Less commonly-used lightred-lightgreen-yellow palette 
(intensity bit set) with a blue background.

CGA_BW.PCX    640x200 B&W pic in case he didn't have a sample.  
Most PCX decoders handle this just fine.

----------------------------------------------------------------------

cga_pb3.pcx is NOT part of Jim Leonard's set and is NOT hardware verified.

All four files above use the PC Paintbrush 4.0 CGA encoding, where colormap
entry 1 holds the approximate RGB of palette color 1. That left the older
PC Paintbrush 3.0 encoding -- three flag bits in colormap[3] (color burst,
palette, intensity) and nothing else -- decoded by no fixture at all.

cga_pb3.pcx fills that gap. It is cga_fsd.pcx's pixel data verbatim with the
48-byte colormap zeroed except colormap[3] = 0x20, i.e. the intensity flag,
selecting palette 1: light green, light red, yellow on a black background.
It must render in those colors, not in cga_fsd.pcx's light cyan / light
magenta / white.

Palette index 0-3 was used deliberately. The color burst palettes (4-7) are
only reachable through the 3.0 encoding, and the encoder can only write the
4.0 form, so a burst palette would not survive TestEncoder's round trip.
Those palettes therefore remain uncovered by any fixture.
